candidate_falsified: the heat-polynomial image is a small exceptional test family whose positivity may avoid the full odd Gaussian-polynomial Weil difficulty
source_map: G_(t,h,p)(u)=exp(-t u^2/2) q_h(u) p(exp(-h u^2)), q_h(u)=u sqrt((1-exp(-h u^2))/u^2)
scaled_limit: q_h(u)/sqrt(h) tends to u as h tends to zero
combined_limit: for p_h(y)=h^(-k)(1-y)^k, G_(t,h,p_h)/sqrt(h) tends to exp(-t u^2/2)u^(2k+1)
density: odd monomial-Gaussians span the odd Hermite sector densely in odd L2; with standard seminorm estimates the convergence is Schwartz
consequence: the union over small h and polynomials is not a protective finite or sparse subspace; positivity extends by continuity to every odd Gaussian-polynomial square
warning: this does not by itself prove density in the entire admissible Weil test topology or establish RH equivalence
acceptance_test: Prove uniform Schwartz-seminorm convergence of the scaled heat-polynomial tests to every odd monomial-Gaussian and identify whether the odd Hermite sector is already a Weil/RH-determining test family.
